nota: 'Exposure to excessive natural heat (X30)' e 'Drowning and submersion while in natural water (W69)'. PENDENTE f180, ACHADO: 'Accidental drowning and submersion (W65-W74)' = 208, 161, 181, 200, 209, 193, 236, 222, 242, 225 = 2,077. A voz diz 'drowning in rivers, lakes and the sea killed more than a thousand': é o W69 (1,010), e não o total (2,077), que inclui banheira e piscina; na tela, os dois só com o rótulo do código. A Table 15.4 tem outro 'Total accidental drowning' (301 em 2025), com transporte e quedas (nota (d)): não misturar.

texto_aprovado: Heat and water kill far more Australians than venom does. Over that same decade, extreme natural heat killed 202 people, and drowning in rivers, lakes and the sea killed more than a thousand. None of that is on the famous list. Neither are the roads we started with.
